sources.title: Floyd cycle Java reproducible boundary and exhaustive functional-graph test
Floyd cycle detection and entry-location reproducible derivation

claims.text: The supplied Java implementation returns false for null and acyclic inputs, true for self and two-node cycles, and agrees with an independent visited-node reference for every four-node functional graph reachable from head (625 next-pointer assignments).

For a finite singly linked list, the documented μ/λ derivation proves that the fast pointer reaches null on an acyclic list and that the two pointers meet within at most n loop iterations on a cyclic list; the implementation therefore has O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space without rewriting next pointers.
The documented derivation proves the stated entry-location follow-up, and derives the HashSet alternative's O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary-space trade-off.

boundary_tests.expected: all 625 next-pointer assignments agree with independent visited-node reference

review_history.finding: Finite exhaustive tests did not cover the candidate's universal correctness, entry-location, and HashSet trade-off claims.
